paper.title: RoboPhD: Self-Improving Text-to-SQL Through Autonomous Agent Evolution
paper.central_claim: AI agents autonomously conduct research in a closed evolution loop (Evolution agent + ELO selection) that improves a Text-to-SQL agent package (Python database-analysis tool + SQL-generation instructions) from a trivial ~70-line baseline to 73.67% on the BIRD test set, with larger gains on cheaper executor models ('skip a tier').

signatures.object: Agent package = tools/*.py database-analysis script + eval_instructions.md (naive baseline: 50-line DDL dump + 20-line instructions)
signatures.information: Evolution AI (Claude Code, Sonnet/Opus 4.5) sees ELO rankings, accuracy, error-analysis report and top agents' packages plus a hand-written cross-pollination strategy; the SQL model sees analysis output ⊕ instructions ⊕ question ⊕ BIRD evidence, never the schema directly; no test data.
signatures.operation: Evolution AI combines techniques of top agents and fixes error patterns into one new package; 'Deep Focus' re-tests the candidate against earlier iterations' questions in the same session and refines (k=1).
signatures.output: One new candidate package per iteration (plus reasoning.md).
signatures.conditions: Tool-only deterministic analysis required; 200K-token context limit forces size-adaptive analysis; Haiku-4.5 is the SQL generator during evolution.
signatures.feedback: Execution accuracy (BIRD set comparison) on 5 random train DBs x 30 questions per iteration.
signatures.selection_rule: Three-way competition (previous winner, new agent, random top-2 ELO), pairwise ELO update K=32; winner by raw accuracy; from iteration 12, 30% of iterations are non-evolution 'challenger/none' rounds.
signatures.persistence: All agent packages and ELO ratings are archived across iterations.
signatures.later_use: Winner and top-ELO agents are the parents shown to the next Evolution AI call; best package is deployed unchanged (analysis run once per DB offline).
signatures.failure_boundary: Single run; champion-selection rule, dev question count and per-iteration variance not reported; no ELO, Deep-Focus or artifact-level ablation.

gap.author_gap: Strong Text-to-SQL systems rely on manual prompt/architecture engineering and domain expertise; the paper wants agents to discover such strategies autonomously.
gap.checked_gap: The manual-engineering cost is a real, but generic, limitation. Related work covers Text-to-SQL systems and prompt optimisers (APE, OPRO, DSPy, TextGrad, ACE) and evolutionary NAS/HPO; code-level agent-evolution neighbours are not discussed in the material, and no head-to-head with any optimiser is given. The 'first ELO for evolutionary prompt/agent optimisation' claim was not checked (no external search).
lineage: prompt optimisers (APE/OPRO/DSPy/TextGrad/ACE) -> evolving complete agent artifacts (tool + instructions)
evolutionary NAS/HPO -> population with ELO rating
closest_adjacent: TextGrad (text-gradient analogy used by the authors)
BIRD leaderboard systems (CHASE-SQL, XiYan-SQL, AskData etc.; manual designs)
gap.residue: Whether LLM-driven evolution of executable analysis tools + instructions beats prompt-only optimisers or strong hand-engineered baselines is untested.
gap.stakes: Engineering effort per domain; cost-per-query tier choice.
gap.method_response: Co-evolve a deterministic analysis tool and instructions via cross-pollination under ELO selection.
gap.remaining_gap: No optimiser baselines, no meta-evolution result, single domain, single run.
unresolved: Nearest-neighbour agent-evolution papers not fixed locally; novelty of ELO selection unchecked.
Whether gains exceed a strong hand-written package of equal length.

rs_pattern.reason: Opus confirms son55. The executed operation is LLM-operator population evolution with ELO selection over a two-artifact agent package (a deterministic analysis script whose output becomes the prompt, plus instruction text) against an execution-accuracy fitness. Run precedent (cal-dev GrIPS, r04b EvoAgentX, r08b 2512.09108): population search over model-input artifacts has no main card. generative_process_redesign (sol) would turn every optimizer into 'liberating a fixed component'. Also rejected: adapt_via_conditioning (no curated cross-iteration experience is read by the executor, opus:O02) and decompose_and_delegate/C25 (it describes only the fixed scaffold analysis→SQL→verification, not the evolved operation). The domain card H14 carries the operation. The paper is fully evaluated regardless.

G.reason: Both seats 2; re-checked. Manual engineering of Text-to-SQL systems is a real limitation. Neighbours are prompt optimizers and BIRD systems; code-level agent-evolution neighbours and an optimizer head-to-head are missing; the residual is not sharply bounded.

M.reason: Both seats 3; re-checked. Error-report-fed proposal, Deep Focus refinement on prior iterations, a persistent ELO archive and same-question head-to-head evaluation form a reasoned response to hand-fixed tool/instruction design. Not 4: no distinguishing prediction against a simpler optimizer is tested, and the non-transitivity rationale for ELO is asserted, not shown.

X.reason: Both seats 3; re-checked. Artifacts, information access, selection protocol (App. D), tool-only interface and deployment are reconstructable. Not 4: the rule that picked the 'Best Evolved' package for dev/test is not stated, and the late-stage challenger schedule is hand-set.

E.measurement.reason: Both seats 3; re-checked. BIRD execution accuracy (set-equivalence) is used throughout; the official test is executed by the BIRD team. Not 4: the per-iteration fitness uses 150 questions (noisy), and the dev denominator is not restated.

E.causality.reason: Both seats 1; re-checked. The only comparison is evolved vs a deliberately trivial naive package on the same executor. There is no ELO/archive, Deep Focus, tool-vs-instructions, alternative-optimizer or strong hand-written control. The strategy comparison is asserted without data. The inverse-scaling claim is confounded by Haiku-based evolution.

E.holdout.reason: Both seats 3; re-checked. Evolution on the 69 train DBs; dev DBs are disjoint; the official test is held and run by the BIRD team. Not 4: the champion-selection rule and any dev use during framework development are unreported, and pretraining contamination of BIRD is not discussed.

E.statistics.reason: Both seats 1; re-checked (A2 ladder). A single evolutionary campaign; the authors acknowledge amplifying non-determinism but give no repeats or intervals. Sample sizes per iteration and a negative sub-result (Simple −0.32) are reported.

E.cost.reason: Opus sides with son55. Per-query cost for all three tiers before/after evolution, $2 and 22 min per iteration, quota share for a 30-iteration run, hardware, and the tool-failure cost share are disclosed. The lower-cost claim is explicitly limited to inference (opus:O01). Not 4: evolution cost is not expressed in tokens/$, and there is no budget-matched alternative optimizer (the missing control is charged to E.causality).
